records.answer:
Based on the knowledge base, here's what HPP means in unsupervised ship/vessel ReID:

## Hard Positive Problem (HPP)

**Definition:** HPP refers to the difficulty of correctly identifying images of the **same vessel identity as positives** during unsupervised training, because the pseudo-labels generated by clustering are inaccurate.

**Why it arises (in the unsupervised vessel ReID context):**

1. **Inaccurate pseudo-labels from clustering.** Maritime vessels have two distinctive characteristics that make clustering unreliable: (a) different vessels in the same super-category (e.g., passenger ships) look very similar, and (b) images of the same vessel captured from different viewpoints usually differ substantially. This makes it challenging to generate accurate pseudo-labels for unlabeled vessel images. As a result, images with the same vessel identity are hard to treat as positives — this is what the paper names the **hard positive problem (HPP)** (source: *Unsupervised Maritime Vessel Re-Identification With Multi-Level Contrastive Learning*, p.2, relevance 0.51/0.37).

2. **Instance-level contrastive loss treats same-pseudo-label images as separate classes.** Even when pseudo-labels exist, conventional instance-level contrastive losses regard images sharing a pseudo-label as distinct classes, making it hard to discover true positives (same source, p.2).

The paper notes these two factors together make unsupervised vessel ReID **more sensitive to HPP than other ReID tasks**.

**Consequences of HPP:**
- It leads to a **uniform feature distribution**, pushing vessel identities away from each other and driving the model into a harder pattern to recover from (source: same paper, p.2 and p.11, relevance 0.44/0.50).
- Once the distance between a positive pair exceeds the **clustering threshold**, those images will **never be clustered together in subsequent epochs** — a self-reinforcing failure (p.11).

**Proposed mitigation:** The paper proposes a **Multi-Level Contrastive Learning (MCL)** framework (no memory bank), including an intra-batch cluster-level contrastive loss and a strategy that excludes potential positives sharing the same pseudo-label from the denominator of the instance-level contrastive loss, thereby pulling positives toward the anchor and effectively solving the HPP (source: same paper, p.2 and p.4).

Note: this concept is defined specifically in the *Unsupervised Maritime Vessel Re-Identification With Multi-Level Contrastive Learning* paper; the other retrieved ship ReID papers (e.g., A²RNet, ViV-ReID) did not discuss HPP in the retrieved passages.
